Subject: Dedicated capacity: Lumen-64k - initial footprint ask

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Asterion is moving toward a reserved-capacity model for our inference workloads and we need a realistic sizing estimate tied to a purchase commitment. High level: we plan to serve a custom fine-tuned variant of "Lumen-64k" (70B-ish architecture) with a 64k context window and a KV cache strategy that keeps long-running sessions responsive.

Traffic profile (early stage):
- P50 concurrent active sessions: 28
- Peak concurrent heavy sessions (long context sampling): 120
- Typical request: 1,200 tokens input + 800 tokens generation (avg)
- Expected 95th token throughput: ~350 rps across the fleet after month-1 ramp

Questions for sizing:
1) Rough GPU footprint per serving instance for fp16 vs int8 vs int4 variants (including KV cache memory)
2) Recommended GPU class (80GB A100 / 80GB H100 / 48GB options) and whether we should plan for KV offload to host or NVMe for 64k windows
3) Ballpark dedicated GPU count for an initial reserved pool (target starting commit) and recommended headroom factor for rollouts

I'm attaching a one-page RFP with the ask and some example prompt mixes. Can you poke at this with a back-of-envelope today/tomorrow? We want something concrete to share with procurement next week.

Attachments: Asterion_RFP_Specs.pdf

Thanks,
Sam Taylor
Head of ML Eng, Asterion Labs

Sam —

Appreciate the detailed RFP. We've pulled a quick preliminary sketch below so you have something to share with procurement. This is intentionally conservative — we'll refine after we profile a representative model checkpoint and a sample prompt corpus.

High-level recommendations (short):
- Start with int8 quantized serving for baseline committed capacity; reserve a small pool of fp16 instances for parity testing and worst-case QA.
- For 64k windows we recommend a hybrid approach: keep the active short context in GPU memory and push cold segments to NVMe-backed KV offload for cost efficiency.
- Suggested initial reserved pool: 18 x 80GB GPUs (see details below). Plan +20% headroom for rollout spikes and canary testing.

Attachments: RDW-prelim-sizing.xlsx (prelim calc & assumptions).

Next steps we need from you:
1) A model checkpoint or a 1-2 minute sample run (can be synthetic) so our infra team can generate a true memory profile.
2) Top-10 prompt templates for realistic token distribution.
3) Contract timeline / target go-live date so we can map procurement milestones.

I'll loop Marcus for cost/ops impacts and Karthik will follow up with the detailed per-instance breakdown. If you want a 45m deep-dive early next week, Marissa can schedule.

Best,

Fwding quick engineering notes so procurement has numbers they can react to. Sam, this is a first-principles pass — we'll tighten after we run the checkpoint.

Summary (key figures):
- Model class: Lumen-64k (approx. 70B)
- Raw weight footprint (approx):
  • fp16: ~140 GB (full raw weights)
  • int8 (dynamic quant): ~45 GB (typical + attention kernel overhead)
  • int4 (aggressive): ~28 GB (higher perf risk)

- KV cache (64k): rough ballpark depending on representation and per-token key/value size. Using our midline assumptions (compact KV with 2x vectors stored):
  • fp16 KV for 64k window: ~72 GB
  • quantized KV (8-bit): ~20–24 GB
  • aggressive KV compression / chunked NVMe: ~8–12 GB resident on GPU + the rest staged to NVMe

- Per-instance GPU sizing (serving instance = model + active KV resident in GPU):
  • fp16-only (no KV offload): impractical on a single 80GB GPU (weights + KV exceed 200GB). Requires sharded multi-GPU serving (4+ x 80GB) — high complexity.
  • int8 w/ partial KV resident: fits on a single 80GB A100/H100 in our runtime with ~10–18GB left for beam/gen state. This is the recommended baseline for reserved instances.
  • int4: more headroom but higher quality risk; can reduce instance count but needs early evals.

- Fleet sizing (initial commit): using your traffic profile and conservative concurrency assumptions:
  • Effective tokens/sec per instance (int8 baseline): ~90–120 tokens/sec (depends on batching & prompt variance).
  • Back-of-envelope: to handle 350 rps (at avg 800 generated tokens), that's ~280k tokens/sec aggregate.
  • Required int8 instances ~= 280k / 100 ≈ 2,800 instance-equivalents of token RPS. With batching and multi-request multiplexing, one physical 80GB GPU can host ~20 instance-equivalents (workload dependent).
  • Physical GPUs needed (initial, rounded) ≈ 2,800 / 20 = 140 GPUs.
  • Recommended starting reserved commit: 140 GPUs (80GB class) with a staged ramp (commit 80 GPUs first + option to add 60 GPUs within 60 days).
  • If you use aggressive KV offload (most cold context on NVMe), PCs drop to ~60–80 GPUs initial (but expect higher NVMe throughput & ops complexity).

Operational notes:
- Headroom: we suggest contractual +20% burst pool for canary/rollouts.
- Fallbacks: maintain a smaller fp16-sharded pool (4-8 GPUs) for QA and deterministic parity.
- Cost trade: int8 baseline reduces committed GPU count dramatically vs fp16 sharded option but requires careful evals to ensure prompt-level quality meets your SLA.

I'll follow up with an attached spreadsheet (RDW-prelim-sizing.xlsx) that contains the math, assumptions, and a sensitivity table (tokens per request, batching efficiency, KV resident percentage). Marcus: please add run-rate cost estimates in the shared sheet — procurement will ask for monthly committed cost + overage rates.

-Karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
